oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: realtime-p99-detector triggered for /v1/streaming/generate — cluster=us-west-2, p99 spike to 2.4s (baseline 0.45s). paging SRE oncall. thread_ts=2719981234
Jordan: ACK — I'm oncall. jumping in. any customer-visible errors?
Maya: saw an uptick in 5xxs for a handful of streaming connections, small percent but p99 skyrocket. dashboard: https://redwood.app/dashboards/realtime-latency?range=5m
Chris: grabbing p95/p99 charts now. looks like spike started ~2719981100 and ramped quickly. p95 ~300ms, p99 ~2.4s.
Alex: any deploys around that time? releasebot:deploys shows no production deploys in last 30m.
Priya: ok start checklist: 1) confirm customer impact 2) check infra pods & queues 3) fallback routing 4) notify product if broader impact
Jordan: customer-impact quick check: sampling error logs for high-latency sessions. run: `kubectl logs -n inference -l app=streaming -f --tail=200 | grep "latency_ms" | tail -n 50`
Chris: pasted small log sample: `{"request_id":"r123","latency_ms":2430,"model":"rlhf-2b-q4"}` repeated 18 times from pod streaming-4
Maya: repeated KV-cache misses? we have a spike in KV cache miss rate for the rl-2b-family. cache hit dropped from 98% to 65% for that window.
Alex: checking node metrics: CPU ~70%, memory normal, but GPU utilization on some nodes is 99%. potential GPU contention on node g-07.
Priya: can we repro with a synthetic trace? Jordan, can you run a few streaming requests to the same variant to see tail behavior?
Jordan: running 5 synthetic stream requests now (token gen load). one of five had a 1.8s stall at token 9. attaching logs.
Jordan: `2026-03-15T17:20:12Z pod=streaming-4 request=r123 stage=kv-fetch duration_ms=1812`
Chris: that looks like an external KV store latency spike. paging infra team to check redis/kv cluster. @Alex can you check kv-metrics?
Alex: on it — `redis-prod-usw2` shows increased avg latency from 1.2ms to 18ms for a short window; some connections queued. suspected transient network blip between inference-subnet and redis-subnet.
Maya: product impacted? product-ops says a minority of sessions saw perceptible delay. I'll prepare an incident update if we escalate.
oncall-bot: page sent to infra-pager (Alex).
Jordan: mitigation plan options: 1) route streaming requests to rl-2b-quantized fallback (lower mem/kernels) 2) enable local in-memory prefix cache for hot keys 3) rate-limit noisy clients 4) restart affected streaming pods to clear stuck KV connections
Priya: go with fastest safe: (1) and (4). Chris, can you flip routing for 10% to fallback and observe? use console quick command: `rbctl route set --service=streaming --variant=rl-2b-q4-small --percent=10`
Chris: applying now. `> rbctl route set --service=streaming --variant=rl-2b-q4-small --percent=10` -> accepted.
Jordan: initiating rolling restart of streaming-4 and streaming-5 pods (kubectl rollout restart deployment/streaming --namespace=inference --selector=pod=streaming-4,streaming-5). will monitor.
Maya: updating incident channel and posting initial customer note: "We are investigating increased latencies for streaming endpoints in us-west-2; small % of requests affected. Oncall triage in progress."
Alex: infra note: Redis team reports a short-lived network flap; they've isolated a noisy VM in the cluster and disabled it. latency back to normal at host level ~2719981305.
Chris: after route change and restarts, p99 dropped from 2.4s -> 0.48s within two minutes. p95 steady ~320ms.
Jordan: continuing monitoring for 15m. keeping the 10% fallback in place for now.
Priya: assign actions: Alex — follow up with redis team and get RCA; Chris — keep routing at 10% and prepare rollback criteria; Maya — draft customer-facing summary if escalation needed; Jordan — run postmortem timeline and logs collection.
Maya: added product and support to watchers, creating incident ticket INC-20260315-27.
Chris: metrics snapshot command for runbook: `curl -s "https://metrics.api/redwood/query?m=p99_latency&service=streaming&range=10m" | jq .`
Jordan: logs archived to s3: s3://redwood-incidents/2719981234/logs.tar.gz
Priya: status update to channel in 10m. if p99 remains < 0.6s and redis latency stable, we'll close the paging.
oncall-bot: Reminder: oncall handoff scheduled in 45m.
Alex: filing infra ticket INF-4529 for host replacement and NIC diagnostics.
Chris: p99 now 0.49s at 2719981388. continuing watch. :thumbsup:
Maya: thanks team — great coordination. will escalate to SEs only if customer impact widens.
Jordan: moving to monitoring phase, will collect final artifacts for postmortem.
Priya: closing notes: cause = transient redis network flap causing higher KV latencies -> tail stalls on streaming kernel path; mitigations = route 10% to quantized fallback + restart affected pods + remove noisy host; next steps = RCA draft + infra remediation ticket.
Chris: marking incident as "mitigated" in tracker but keeping ticket open for RCA.
Maya: final update to customer (if needed) prepared and awaiting review.
Jordan: last_message_ts=2719981400"
